Context from a materials paper:
- Mechanisms behind the orientation dependence (anisotropy) of SLM IN718 mechanical properties have not been discussed in detail
- IN718 superalloy processed by SLM from pre-alloyed powder
- SLM build of IN718 cubes layer by layer with a shifting/rotating scan strategy
- Grains are columnar along BD, spanning several layers, in side sections and near-equiaxed in top sections
- Side-disc columnar grains lie across the load, rotate during bulging and put slip systems near 45 deg (high Schmid factor), raising dislocation multiplication and work hardening; top-disc grains stay parallel to load (low Schmid factor)

Panels:
- F6c: caption: Fig. 6. EBSD orientation maps of SLM-fabricated IN718 for the ... side and
- F6d: caption: Fig. 6. EBSD orientation maps of SLM-fabricated IN718 for the ... top cross-sections

Question: The claim under test holds that side-disc columnar grains rotate during bulging so their slip systems sit near 45 degrees to the load (high Schmid factor), while top-disc grains stay parallel to the load (low Schmid factor). Panels F6c and F6d give the {100} pole figures for the side and top discs. What do these pole figures show about the crystallographic direction of the punch (disc-normal) axis in each disc?

key.answer_key: The side and top {100} pole figures show the same cube pattern in their own disc frames, so the disc-normal (punch) axis is a <100> direction for both specimens.
